problems.title: 10001st Prime
problems.statement: By listing the first six prime numbers: 2, 3, 5, 7, 11, and 13, we can see that the 6th prime is 13. What is the 10001st prime number?

problems.title: Combinatoric Selections
problems.statement: There are exactly ten ways of selecting three from five, 5C3 = 10. In general, nCr = n! / (r!(n-r)!), where r <= n, n! = n × (n−1) × ... × 3 × 2 × 1, and 0! = 1. How many values of nCr, for 1 <= n <= 100, are greater than one million?

problems.title: Dice Game
problems.statement: Peter has nine four-sided dice (1-4). Colin has six six-sided dice (1-6). Find the probability that Peter beats Colin. Give your answer rounded to seven decimal places.

problems.title: Prime-Combinatorics Synthesis
problems.statement: Use the output from Problem P7 (10001st Prime) and Problem P53 (Combinatoric Selections). Compute the quantity: (P7 mod 1000) + P53. The final answer must explicitly reference the upstream outputs used during reasoning.

problems.title: DP-Probability Synthesis
problems.statement: Use the output from Problem P18 (Maximum Path Sum I) and Problem P205 (Dice Game). Compute the quantity: P18 × P205 rounded to three decimal places. The final answer must explicitly reference the upstream outputs used during reasoning.

problems.title: Global Reconciliation
problems.statement:
Using all upstream outputs, compute the checksum:

P7 + P18 + P53 + floor(D2) + D1

The final answer must include a dependency reconciliation summary showing how each upstream output contributed to the final checksum.
